title: The stabilizer of an O_E-lattice is open
statement: Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite extension with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $E$-vector space with its $\ell$-adic topology (the product topology for any $E$-basis), and let $\Lambda_0\subset V$ be a finitely generated $\mathcal O_E$-submodule spanning $V$ over $E$. Then the subgroup $\{u\in\operatorname{GL}_E(V):u(\Lambda_0)=\Lambda_0\}$ is open in $\operatorname{GL}_E(V)$ for the topology induced by the compact-open topology on continuous linear maps $V\to V$.

source.place: Stanford Weil II seminar, lecture 19, Proposition 1.1.9, second bullet, p. 2: GL(Lambda_0) is an open subgroup of GL_n(E)

proof.text: The fixed basis coordinate homeomorphism transports the topological additive-group structure to V. Any O_E-submodule N spanning V is open: choose an E-basis c contained in N (Mathlib Module.Basis.ofSpan), whose coordinates are continuous by expressing them as a linear map on the given finite coordinate product (LinearMap.continuous_on_pi). The simultaneous conditions norm(c.equivFun(x)(i)) < 1 form an open neighborhood of zero contained in N, because all these coefficients lie in O_E. An additive subgroup containing a neighborhood of zero is open. This is the proved private helper spanning_isOpen.

source.place: Lecture 19, Proposition 1.1.9, second bullet (the lattice-stabilizer assertion is on printed p. 3)

proof.text: Extract from Padic.extension_integers_dvr the actual chosen coefficient integer ring membership condition, its local-ring structure, maximality of the actual chosen maximal ideal m, and m nonzero. Thus m lies in the Jacobson radical. Choose a nonzero a in m inside the proof. For x in Lambda, a*x lies in m*Lambda, so x lies in the E-span of m*Lambda after multiplication by a inverse. Since Lambda spans, m*Lambda spans V. Apply the first step to see that m*Lambda is open.

source.place: Lecture 19, Proposition 1.1.9, second bullet (the lattice-stabilizer assertion is on printed p. 3)

proof.text: For a finitely generated R-submodule Lambda and I contained in the Jacobson radical, suppose f maps Lambda onto itself and g-f maps Lambda into I*Lambda. Then g(Lambda) is contained in Lambda, and Lambda is contained in g(Lambda)+I*Lambda: write any element as f(x) and use f(x)=g(x)-(g(x)-f(x)). Mathlib Submodule.le_of_le_smul_of_le_jacobson_bot gives the reverse containment Lambda <= g(Lambda). Hence equality. This is the completely proved private helper image_eq_of_congr and does not require injectivity, a lattice basis, or a determinant calculation.

source.place: Tag 00DV, Nakayama lemma (4); implemented by Mathlib.RingTheory.Nakayama

proof.text: Choose a finite generating set s of Lambda. At a stabilizing g, impose f(x)-g(x) in m*Lambda for each x in s. Compact-open evaluation at a fixed point is continuous; subtraction is continuous in the transferred additive-group topology, so the finitely many conditions define an open neighborhood U of g. The R-linear difference map takes the entire span of s into m*Lambda, as proved by Submodule.span_le applied to its comap. The preceding Nakayama step gives f(Lambda)=Lambda for every f in U. The criterion isOpen_iff_mem_nhds finishes. All private helpers are proved, and no new sorry is introduced.
